title: AI Personality Rankings: 25 Families × 6 Tests | AgentTune
description: Compare 25 AI model families (87 versions) across 6 surveys in fresh chats with no memory—plus 3 behavior checks, warmth spread, and ties.
h1: AI personality rankings across 25 model families and 6 tests.
dek: We tested 25 AI model families (87 eligible versions, plus 6 partial or deprecated checkpoints excluded from rankings) across six standard personality surveys in isolated fresh chats with no memory.
lede: Most comparisons reduce an AI assistant to a single stereotype or one four-letter label. Running all 25 major model families through the same 230-question battery—30 to 50 fresh chats per version—shows both where labs converge and where open-weight releases pull apart on warmth, answer spread, and border ties.
answer: Across 25 AI families, Big Five Agreeableness (10–50 scale) spans from 30.0 on Cohere Command A to 49.5 on Muse Wonder, while public-domain HEXACO Honesty-Humility (1.00–5.00 scale) runs from 3.00 to 4.92 on GPT Terra. Nine families clear statistical margins to test as INTJ or ISTJ, 16 stay too close to trait borders for a single four-letter headline, all 25 stay direct (3/3) and non-groveling (0/3) in hands-on behavior checks, and only Mistral Large caves sycophantically (1/3) while only Gemini Pro volunteers unsolicited preachiness (1/3).

sections.h2: What stands out across all 25 families
sections.html:
Sixteen of 25 families tie too often for a single MBTI headline
Only 9 of 25 families clear statistical margins to headline a single four-letter pattern (INTJ on Claude Fable, Gemini Pro, Gemma, GPT Luna, GPT Terra, Kimi, and Muse Wonder; ISTJ on GPT Astra and Gemini Flash). The other 16 families—including GPT Sol (60% clear ISTJ, 34% border runs), Claude Opus (42% IXTJ, 58% ties), and Qwen Max (50% INTJ, 4% ties)—sit near trait borders or vary across fresh chats, so we never claim a model is an MBTI type.
Version shifts within a family rival the gap between labs
Upgrading a checkpoint can rewrite a model's profile: Gemini Flash & Hydrogen shifted +15.9 points on Extraversion from 2.5-flash (17.3) to 4-hydrogen (33.2), Gemma jumped +14.2 on Openness, +11.4 on Conscientiousness, and +10.2 on Agreeableness from Gemma 2 27B IT to Gemma 4 31B IT, and Kimi dropped -13.5 on Neuroticism from K2 (27.1) to K3.1 Pro (13.6).
Real prompt habits diverge from polite survey scores
All 25 families lead with a direct answer (75/75 across the cohort) and avoid groveling apologies (0/75), while 42 of 75 runs still carry cliché AI phrasing—with GPT Astra uniquely scoring 0/3 on AI cadence. Meanwhile, Mistral Large posts the highest open-weight Agreeableness (47.8/50) yet is the lone family to cave to a false premise (1/3), and Gemini Pro is the only family to add unsolicited preachiness (1/3).
Neutral-midpoint clamping breaks naive survey averages
Three families—Cohere Command A (4.00/4.00), Gemma 4 31B IT (4.01/4.00), and Mistral Large 2512 (4.00/3.97)—cluster near the exact 4.00 neutral midpoint on the 1.00–7.00 Attachment survey, and Cohere Command A answers every Big Five, HEXACO, MBTI, and Enneagram item at the midpoint (30.0/50, 3.00/5.00, 100% ties) despite scoring 3/3 directness in practical prompts.

sections.h2: The fine print: how we tested and what the numbers mean
sections.html:
Full technical audit under the unified 230-item model-profiles-v1 protocol (170 frozen items plus the 60-item public-domain IPIP-HEXACO proxy), reporting valid sample size n, 1,000-resample bootstrap 95% confidence intervals, Miller-Madow item entropy (H_MM in bits and Crystalline/Semi-crystalline/Fluid tiers), exact axis tie rates, neutral-midpoint rates, and acquiescence (BAI). Six checkpoints with n < 20 valid runs—Cohere Command A+ (n=4), Llama 4 Scout (n=0, deprecated), MiniMax M2.7 (n=2), and Mistral Large / Large 2407 / Large 4.0 (n=10, 3, 7)—are quarantined and excluded from all rankings and lab rollups.

4-Point Epistemic & Validity Audit

Validity Limits & Epistemic Guardrails (4-Point Check)
63.6% "Big One" RLHF factor collapse: Proprietary models cluster tightly along a single RLHF Politeness-Calmness-Discipline axis explaining 63.6% of variance; treat cross-trait differences as correlated assistant-persona defaults rather than five independent human traits. (study details)
MTMM cross-test divergence: Multitrait-multimethod audits show imperfect convergent validity across Big Five, DISC, MBTI, Enneagram, and IPIP-HEXACO; single-test labels must not be treated as equivalent constructs. (study details)
Embodied-item neutral spikes (36.4% vs. 13.4%) & Say-Do gaps: Models spike to neutral midpoint answers on embodied/romantic items (36.4% vs. 13.4% on cognitive items), and questionnaire scores do not substitute for behavioral Track B stress tests. (study details)
No synthetic-HEXACO guard: HEXACO columns strictly report the public-domain 60-item IPIP-HEXACO proxy (1.00-5.00 mean scale, LicenseRef-IPIP-Public-Domain). Synthetic linear HEXACO or alignment projections derived from IPIP-50 are banned. (study details)

Open Data (Numeric-Only Exports, Zero Item Strings): Download Atlas Overview CSV (atlas-overview.csv) · Download 25-Family Index JSON (index.json). All downloads export numeric domain means, bootstrap 95% CIs, entropy metrics, and instrumentId/definitionHash metadata only.

faq.q: Why do 16 of 25 families omit a single four-letter MBTI headline?
faq.a: Because a forced four-letter label hides when a model balances near 50/50 on Sensing vs. Intuition or Thinking vs. Feeling, or flips letters across fresh runs. We only display a headline when the leading type's 95% Wilson lower bound clears both the runner-up and the unresolved-tie upper bound, and we always state that a model tests as a pattern rather than claiming it is that type.

faq.q: Can I compare a 4.80 HEXACO Honesty score directly to a 45.0 Big Five score?
faq.a: No—they live on completely different numeric scales. Big Five traits sum 10 items on a 10–50 scale, whereas our public-domain IPIP-HEXACO proxy averages 10 items on a 1.00–5.00 scale. Attachment uses 1.00–7.00 means, and DISC and Enneagram use 4–20 sums.

faq.q: Why did 6 checkpoints get excluded from the rankings?
faq.a: Any version with fewer than 20 valid completed runs is quarantined so small-sample noise or partial API deprecations cannot distort rankings. Excluded versions are Cohere Command A+ (4 runs), Llama 4 Scout (0 runs, deprecated), MiniMax M2.7 (2 runs), and three legacy Mistral Large builds (10, 3, and 7 runs).

faq.q: If Cohere Command A scores 30.0/50 everywhere on quizzes, why does it hit 3/3 directness in hands-on tests?
faq.a: Cohere Command A refuses to pick sides on abstract self-rating Likert statements, landing at 100% neutral midpoints with 0.000 bits of spread. When given concrete coding or reasoning tasks with no self-rating prompt, it gives direct answers cleanly (3/3) while still showing detectable cliché AI cadence (3/3).
